title: Amman inner-city BRT Lines 1 & 2 operational
summary_2_lines: Two dedicated-lane BRT lines ~32 km: Line 2 (17 km) Sweileh-Jordan Museum, Line 1 (15 km) Al Mahatta-Sweileh. Infrastructure works largely completed by 2024.
notes: Feeder roads connect corridors to Khalda/Dabouq/Sweifieh. Source frames BRT as improving accessibility; no explicit quantified price effect stated.

title: Amman-Zarqa intercity BRT
summary_2_lines: 20 km dedicated BRT corridor central Amman (Al Mahatta) to Zarqa incl. road widening, bridges, tunnels. ~86% complete late-June 2026; trial operations May 2024.
notes: Official MOT project page. Indirectly benefits NE Amman via improved commuting.

title: Planned BRT extension Sweileh-QAIA via King Abdullah II St
summary_2_lines: GAM studying ~42 km BRT extension from Sweileh Circle to Queen Alia International Airport via King Abdullah II Street. Part of ~3.47bn JOD transport package.
notes: Study phase per Feb 2024 mayor statement. Would reinforce West Amman connectivity.

title: Medical City Bridge / Sweileh-Naour elevated corridor
summary_2_lines: Planned 15.8 km elevated road Safout-Naour integrating public/private traffic and a BRT lane. Announced 2026 in transport-investment package.
impact_area: West Amman incl. Khalda, Dabouq, Naour
notes: Detailed timelines still under development. Source links project to improved traffic flow / investment attractiveness (not a quantified price effect).

title: New Abdali Phase 2 mixed-use expansion
summary_2_lines: ~1.2 million m2 second-phase expansion: conference facilities for 25,000, two hotel/residential towers, medical facilities, added to existing Abdali mall/towers.
notes: Announced May 2024. Overall Abdali master plan >3 million m2 built-up. Intensifies mixed-use central axis between Abdoun and Abdali.

title: GAM district construction & urban upgrades
summary_2_lines: GAM completed ~3.04 million JOD of works by late-2025 (56,467 m2 sidewalks/medians, 3,589 m3 retaining walls, 11,130 m culverts); +500,000 m2 paving announced.
notes: Affects multiple districts; supports overall infrastructure quality / residential values city-wide.

title: 2024 Cabinet registration-fee exemption & property-tax reduction
summary_2_lines: Partial registration-fee exemption for apartments >150 m2, full exemption for smaller first-time-buyer units, and reduced property tax for three years.
expected_effect: +19% apartment sales in late-2024 (credited by DLS)
notes: expected_effect quoted directly from source: DLS credits a 19% increase in apartment sales to these incentives.

title: Jordan real-estate trading volume 7.179bn JOD in 2025
summary_2_lines: Total 2025 trading volume ~7.179bn JOD, +7% vs 2024; revenue +5%. Early-2026 cooling: Jan 2026 volume ~513m JOD, -6% YoY, apartment sales -16%.
notes: Aggregate market direction (grew 2024-25, cooled early-2026). Jan-2026 detail cross-cited to Jordan News.

title: ARPI / CBJ price indices show modest apartment appreciation
summary_2_lines: ARPI (private, 30k+ bank-verified transactions, 58 variables) shows Amman residential ~102 in Q3 2025, rebound to 104 Q1 2026; +1.96% over 12 months to mid-2026.
notes: CBJ Real Estate Price Index (2012=100, Laspeyres) is the only official time series. ARPI commentary flags Abdali & Abdoun as showing continued price strength.

title: Abdoun premium drivers: diplomatic core, views, malls
summary_2_lines: Abdoun is the diplomatic/embassy core of West Amman with limestone architecture, security, city/panoramic hillside views and walkability to Taj Mall & Abdoun Circle.
notes: Qualitative price driver row. View quality, high floor, new build w/ parking+elevator, embassy/expat tenant base raise pricing power.

title: Dabouq premium drivers: green villa zoning, royal proximity, calm
summary_2_lines: Dabouq is an elite low-density villa enclave near royal residences; strict green/villa zoning (often 39% construction cap) enforces calm, privacy and panoramic views.
notes: Qualitative driver row. Scarcity of large plots + inelastic ultra-wealthy demand = capital-preservation market. URL is the Homes-Jordan Dabouq guide (path inferred from title; verify).

title: Sweifieh: commercial noise suppresses sale, boosts rental yield
summary_2_lines: Sweifieh is a walkable commercial anchor (malls, retail corridors). Traffic/noise/congestion suppress residential SALE prices but push small-furnished-unit RENTAL yields to city-highs.
notes: Qualitative driver row: yield-compression / cash-flow archetype. Quieter side streets command residential premium vs congested frontages.

title: Khalda: quiet family suburb, schools, price/convenience balance
summary_2_lines: Khalda is a family-oriented suburban district with wide streets, easy parking, good schools and arterial access; low tenant turnover and utilitarian price/m2 efficiency.
notes: Qualitative driver row. Proximity to intl schools & King Abdullah II St; larger units, parking, elevators drive intra-area variation.

title: Shmeisani: central business district, aging stock, corporate tenants
summary_2_lines: Shmeisani is a traditional business/finance district (banks, hotels, corporate HQs). Older large-floorplan stock trades at a discount; central location draws corporate renters.
notes: Qualitative driver row. Renovation/age is the dominant valuation swing; centrality + parking are premium factors; redevelopment arbitrage opportunity.
